title: China And St. Augustine
text:
China And St. Augustine

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 23 Oct 2026

Back in the summer of 2015, the Chinese government decided that equity markets had risen too far, too fast. The rug was pulled from under margin lending and various restrictions were put in place that brought the unfolding raging equity bull market to an abrupt end. By January 2024, the Chinese government reversed course and decided that Chinese equity prices had fallen far enough. Beijing intervened in the market (see Chinese Policies And Chinese Equities) and put a floor under domestic markets. Equities duly rallied, delivering very solid returns for 2024 and 2025. However, over the past year, Chinese equity market returns have been fairly dismal. In fact, Chinese equity markets have now fallen for 10 consecutive weeks, a feat they had never achieved before. This in spite of the fact that (a) excitement over all things “artificial intelligence” has been a key driver of global equity market performance and that (b) China is one of the few countries outside of the US actually registering notable gains on the AI front. In short, Chinese equities have had a very disappointing month, quarter, year-to-date and 12 months and what had been steady outperformance has now melted away like snow in the sun.
